problem: Prior object-goal navigation methods build object relation graphs from single-frame observations (ORG, VTNet, DOA), use coarse zone graphs (HOZ), or need many exploration steps (SSCNav). They also store or use trajectory history only superficially, so agents forget past observations and get stuck in deadlocks.
motivation: Finding a target in an unseen room needs prior knowledge of category layout, such as a microwave near a stove or sink, and memory of what was already observed. The paper's observation is that a global category graph learned across many observations, plus attention over the trajectory history, gives a richer visual representation for RL policy learning.
key_idea: Learn a global category-level relation graph (CRG) through a learnable adjacency matrix, build a per-step graph sequence from it, and process the sequence with Temporal-Spatial-Region attention (TSR) to produce the visual representation for an A3C policy.
insight: The ablation shows the two parts are complementary. CRG alone lifts SR from 66.2 to 75.2, TSR alone lifts it to 76.4 (SPL 0.452), and the full model reaches 80.0 SR. Removing Region attention hurts most (SR 76.5, SPL 0.419), so linking the graph to image regions matters. A graph sequence length of 4 is best, and longer sequences add noise. A self-learned adjacency (parameter dictionary) beats distance, attention and recurrent graph variants (Graph variants SR 77.5-78.3 vs 80.0). Pre-training with a Dijkstra expert speeds convergence.
method: Detection and depth: DETR gives boxes, confidence, label and appearance features per object; SARPN depth estimation, averaged in the box, gives object depth.

Category Relation Graph: N=22 category nodes with features (box, label, confidence, depth, appearance). The adjacency A=Softmax(ReLU(E1 E2^T)) is learned from two node-embedding dictionaries. A GCN gives Z=ReLU(AXW), with absent categories zeroed. Z from the last L steps forms a graph sequence.
Temporal attention: per-category multi-head self-attention over the L-step sequence with temporal position embedding, followed by SDGCN across nodes.

Spatial attention: MHA with the current graph Z_t as query and the temporal output as key/value, with node position embedding, then SDGCN. The appearance features are re-weighted by A, and the result is concatenated with the box/confidence/depth/label features and the graph features.

Region attention: ResNet18 global feature with positional embedding goes through masked MHA and then cross-attention over the graph representation (key/value), plus a feed-forward layer, giving the final visual representation F.
Policy learning: an LSTM plus A3C actor-critic, 16 workers, 2M episodes, reward -0.01 per step and +5 on success.
Pre-training: the representation extractor plus an MLP is trained with cross-entropy on Dijkstra expert actions for faster convergence.

setting.backbone: DETR detector, SARPN depth, ResNet18 (ImageNet pretrained), GCN/SDGCN + multi-head attention, LSTM + A3C (trained)
setting.training_data: RL in AI2-THOR (20 scenes per room type for training) for 2M episodes, plus a supervised pre-training set of Dijkstra expert trajectories; SARPN depth pre-trained on NYU-Depth v2
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (with estimated depth of detected objects)
setting.action_space: discrete low-level: MoveAhead (0.25 m), RotateLeft/Right (45°), LookUp/Down (30°), Done
setting.privileged: none at test time (the Dijkstra expert is used only for pre-training)

results: CRG-TSR reaches SR 80.0 and SPL 0.456 on AI2-THOR with only 2M training episodes, versus the strongest baselines PONI (SR 79.6) and VTNet (SPL 0.449). It improves over its baseline by +20.8% SR and +29.5% SPL, and on the offline RoboTHOR it gets SR 16.2 versus 12.5 for ACRG.
limitations: Fails on specular reflections such as mirrors: the agent tries to walk into the mirrored space.
Evaluated only in AI2-THOR and an offline RoboTHOR version, with a fixed set of 22 categories and the same category set in training and test rooms; the attention head/layer search was not exhaustive.
Relies on pre-trained DETR and monocular depth estimation, and the results are small in margin over the strongest baselines (80.0 vs 79.6 SR).
